The chapters of the Athlone Joint Urban Settlement Strategy have been 
drafted and are currently being reviewed by both Westmeath and

EMRA RSES Review 
The Planning Authority prepared a comprehensive submission to the RSES 
review, with particular focus on the provision of policy support to facilitate 
the continued growth of Athlone as the Midlands Regional Growth Centre 
as well as Mullingar as a Key Town together with the development of the 
remaining settlements and rural areas of the County. A number of key 
themes were explored in the submission such as expediting the delivery of 
key enabling infrastructure,  the need for collaboration between Local 
Authorities, State and Semi-State bodies to progress the delivery of projects 
of Regional interest, including Columb Barracks and St. Loman's Hospital, 
the Lough Ree & its island as an UNESCO Biosphere Nature Reserve and the 
Hill of Uisneach together with the Royal Sites for UNESCO World Heritage 
designation. 
Residential Zoned 
Land Tax (RZLT) 
The Annual Draft Residential Zoned Land Tax Map was published for 
Westmeath on 01 February 2026 and identifies land that may be liable for 
the tax in 2027. 
In total, 7 no. submissions were received by the Council in relation to the 
Final RZLT Map 2026 comprising of re-zoning requests and 6 no. 
submissions in relating to the Annual RZLT Map for the 2027 liability year. 
The Planning Department assessed the submissions and prepared 
determination reports which issued to landowners on 30 June 2026. It was 
determined that that 4 (no.) parcels of lands did not satisfy the relevant 
criteria specified under Section 653B(a) of the Taxes Consolidation Act 
1997, and therefore it was recommended that they be removed from the 
Draft Annual RZLT Map for the 2027 liability year. 
Landowners can appeal the decision of the Council in relation to the Annual 
Draft RZLT Map to An Coimisiún Pleanála by 01 August 2026.

Westmeath 
Biodiversity Action 
Plan 2025-2031 
The Westmeath Biodiversity Action Plan 2025–2031 was formally 
launched on 15 May 2026 as part of the opening event for National 
Biodiversity Week. The launch marked a significant milestone in the 
implementation of biodiversity actions across the county and was 
attended by stakeholders, community groups and members of the public. 
2026 
Biodiversity 
Week  
National Biodiversity Week 2026 took place during 15-24 May and was a 
significant success, with 20 biodiversity events and workshops delivered 
across the county, including six biodiversity-themed library events. The 
programme included workshops, guided walks, talks and community 
engagement activities focusing on pollinators, butterflies, bats, peatlands, 
invasive species, hedgerows, biodiversity meadows, seed saving and nature 
awareness. 
The events were delivered in partnership with community groups, 
environmental organisations and local stakeholders and provided valuable 
opportunities for public engagement, biodiversity education and 
participation in nature conservation activities.

This forum acts as a collaborative network and working group, bringing together 
representatives of key stakeholders and service providers at management level from 
mainstream services, NGO, and community and voluntary organisations. The role of the

community-led response to support the integration of the relevant cohorts in the Local 
Authority Area.

4.9. Rural Support Schemes 
CLÁR 2026 
CLÁR 2026 was launched in quarter one. Changes in the CLÁR scheme included an 
extension of the CLÁR areas with 4 new areas in Westmeath. The CLÁR areas are 
identified by Electoral Divisions (EDs). The new EDs  are Clonfad, Kinturk, Kilbixy and 
Raharney. These new EDs encompass a number of townlands and areas not previously 
covered by CLÁR and the additions are welcomed. 14 applications were submitted under 
CLÁR 2026 with a grant of max €65,000 for 12 applications and up to €100,000 for two 
applications. 
Outdoor Recreation Infrastructure Scheme (ORIS) 
The ORI scheme for 2026 was launched at the beginning of June. The focus of ORIS is to 
support outdoor recreational infrastructure in countryside areas across Ireland that not 
only provides an outlet for the communities in which they are situated but also delivers 
added value from a tourism perspective. Six applications under M1 for a max grant of 
€40k, 3 applications under M2 for a max grant of €200k and 1 application under M3 for a 
max grant of €500k can be submitted. Also, up to 3 applications can be submitted under 
the Project Development Measure with a combined max grant of €100k. Submission 
dates are in September and December for different Measures.

Road Safety: 
 
Speed Limit Review 
 
The Road Traffic Act 2024 provides for the phased lowering of speed limits in Ireland.  
 
Phase 1.      A reduction in the default speed limit on rural local roads from 80km/h to 60km/h.   
Phase 2.      The introduction of a 30km/h speed limit in built-up and urban areas.   
Phase 3.      A reduction in the speed limit on national secondary roads from 100km/h to 80km/h. 
Phase 4.      The introduction of reduced speed limits adjacent to schools in rural areas.  
 
Phase 1 – Rural Local Roads 
 
The first phase, the change in the default speed limit on rural local roads from 80km/h to 60km/h 
commenced in 2024 and this lowered default speed limit came into effect on the 7th February 2025.   
 
In 2024, Westmeath County Council completed a review in accordance with section 9 of the Road 
Traffic Act of 2004, for our rural local roads. Following completion of this first phase review, no 
amendments to the existing byelaws were required; the new national default speed limit of 60km/h 
was applied to all rural local roads in County Westmeath.  
 
Phase 2 – Built-up and Urban Areas 
 
The second phase of the proposed speed limit changes concerns the introduction of a 30km/h speed 
limit in urban areas. This speed limit change will be introduced by way of ‘special speed limit bye-
laws, rather than a change in the ‘default speed limit’. Accordingly, in respect of those roads in urban 
areas where local authorities propose to change existing speed limits to 30km/h, it will be necessary 
for each local authority to undertake a statutory public consultation process and consider 
representations, in accordance with the requirements of the ‘Road Traffic Act 2004’, as amended. As 
the making of ‘special speed limit bye-laws is a reserved function, the speed limits on roads in urban 
areas will only be changed where a majority of the elected members vote to do so. 
 
To assist local authorities with the second phase, Chapters 4 & 7 of the ‘Guidelines for Setting and 
Managing Speed Limits in Ireland have been updated. Westmeath County Council commenced the 
review process of all built-up & urban areas in Q1 2026. Specific targets for implementation are: 
 
-
